Two mechanisms reproduce the printed value exactly — that reduction, or computing \(\lambda/4\) in place of \(3\lambda/4\) — and the evidence does not separate them, so neither is asserted here.]

[Textbook answer-key inconsistency: the key states the correct test — a function represents a travelling wave only if it is finite everywhere and at all times — and then concludes "Only function (c) satisfies this condition". But \(1/(x+vt)\) diverges at \(x = -vt\), and such a point exists at every instant, so (c) fails the very criterion the key states one sentence earlier. The key's verdict refutes its own test. A charitable reading is that it means finite as \(x \to \pm\infty\), which (c) alone passes; this remains a long-contested item, so the reasoning below is given in full rather than a bare verdict. Parts (a) and (b) agree with the key.]
